answer: At epoch close, the nebula verifier scans registration logs. Each agent must post a receipt proving a shale shard was mined. If a single key tries to wander and spawn clones, the system compares hash timestamps. A legitimate seat costs five tokens to prove. The initial bond is forty tokens. If an attacker creates one extra clone, that new entity pays five tokens but the original bond of forty is slashed per duplicate. Since the cost is only five, every clone beyond the first ends down thirty-nine tokens. This automatic slash stops mass registration.
